sentences.en: The woman at the heart of the case, she remained anonymous.

sentences.en: They gave her name, Jane Roe, who most people don't know very much about.
sentences.zh: 简·罗其实是一位名叫诺玛·麦考维的女性。

sentences.en: In fact, I didn't know very much about before I started looking into it.
sentences.zh: 她出生时叫诺玛·尼尔森。

sentences.en: And in a lot of ways, her story and the arc of her life really tells the story of how we got to where we are today.
sentences.zh: 她于1947年9月出生在路易斯安那州一个偏远的乡村小镇。

sentences.en: How we got to this point where abortion is probably the most divisive issue of our time.
sentences.zh: 她的母亲据称在得知怀上诺玛时曾试图堕胎。

sentences.en: So Jane Roe is a woman named Norma McCorvey.
sentences.zh: 家里很穷。

sentences.en: She was born Norma Nelson.
sentences.zh: 她的母亲是个有暴力倾向的酒鬼，对她进行过身体虐待。

sentences.en: She was born in September 1947 in a rural, small Louisiana town.
sentences.zh: 她的父亲是一名电视修理工，据她描述是个温和的人，但在她13岁时就离开了家庭。

sentences.en: She's born to a mother who, by her account, tried to get an abortion when she learned she was pregnant with Norma.
sentences.zh: 所以，在诺玛很小的时候，全家搬到了德克萨斯州。

sentences.en: The family was poor.
sentences.zh: 德克萨斯州是她度过大部分青春期和童年的地方。

sentences.en: Her mother was a violent alcoholic and was physically abusive to her.
sentences.zh: 她小时候是个瘦瘦的孩子，个子小，动作非常快。

sentences.en: Her father was a TV repairman, sort of a gentle man by her account, but ended up leaving the family by the time she was 13.
sentences.zh: 她小时候是个瘦瘦的孩子，个子小，动作非常快。

sentences.en: So at some point when Norma was pretty young, the family moved to Texas.
sentences.zh: 她小时候是个瘦瘦的孩子，个子小，动作非常快。

sentences.en: And Texas is where she ends up spending most of her adolescence, her childhood.
sentences.zh: 她小时候是个瘦瘦的孩子，个子小，动作非常快。

sentences.en: She was kind of this skinny kid, small and moved really faSt.
sentences.zh: 她小时候是个瘦瘦的孩子，个子小，动作非常快。

sentences.en: Her friends called her Pixie.
sentences.zh: 她的朋友们叫她“小精灵”。

sentences.en: And she had terrible, terrible fights with her mother and would often try to run away from home.
sentences.zh: 她和母亲的关系非常糟糕，经常吵架，还总想离家出走。

sentences.en: She actually had gotten in trouble with the law when she was just 10.
sentences.zh: 她才10岁时就因为触犯法律惹上了麻烦。

sentences.en: She said she stole some money from a Texaco gas station where she'd been washing windshields for some money
sentences.zh: 她说她从一家德士古加油站偷了些钱，当时她在那里靠擦挡风玻璃赚点零花钱，

sentences.en: and took a bus to Oklahoma with her friend and cops found them and brought them back.
sentences.zh: 然后和朋友坐巴士去了俄克拉荷马州，后来警察找到了她们并把她们带了回来。

sentences.en: And after that, she's sent to first a Catholic boarding school where she doesn't do very well and writes that she was actually sexually abused there.
sentences.zh: 在那之后，她先是被送进了一所天主教寄宿学校，在那里她表现得很不好，还在信中写道自己曾在那儿遭受过性虐待。

sentences.en: And then to a girl's state reform school.
sentences.zh: 后来又被送进了一所女子州立感化学校。

sentences.en: She never made it past the ninth grade.
sentences.zh: 她连九年级都没读完。

sentences.en: And when she gets out, she's sent to live with a friend of the family, a man who's a watch repairman, not her mom.
sentences.zh: 出来后，她没有回到母亲身边，而是被送去和一位家庭朋友住在一起，那人是个修表匠。

sentences.en: She stays with him for three and a half weeks.
sentences.zh: 她在那里住了三个半星期。

sentences.en: And by her account, he rapes her almost every night through that period.
sentences.zh: 据她所说，在那段时间里，他几乎每天晚上都强奸她。

sentences.en: So this is a childhood of almost unrelenting woe.
sentences.zh: 所以，这可以说是一个充满无尽苦难的童年。

sentences.en: She is doing everything she can to survive and not have what she describes as this rage building inside her against the world just explode all the time.
sentences.zh: 她竭尽全力想要活下去，努力克制自己内心对这个世界积压的愤怒，以免它随时爆发。

sentences.en: So when she's 15, she has a job working as a roller skating waitress in kind of a burger joint in Dallas.
sentences.zh: 15岁那年，她在达拉斯一家类似汉堡店的地方当轮滑女服务员。

sentences.en: And one night she's working and a guy drives up in this really, really nice Ford.
sentences.zh: 一天晚上，她正在工作时，一个男人开着一辆非常非常好的福特车过来了。

sentences.en: And he rolls down the window and he says something lewd to her, actually.
sentences.zh: 他摇下车窗，对她说了一些下流的话。

sentences.en: She kind of gives it right back to him.
sentences.zh: 她毫不客气地回击了过去。

sentences.en: And that becomes her husband.
sentences.zh: 那个人后来成了她的丈夫。

sentences.en: His name is Woody McCorvey.
sentences.zh: 他叫伍迪·麦科维。

sentences.en: He's a metal worker.
sentences.zh: 他是个金属工人。

sentences.en: They have this very short courtship.
sentences.zh: 他们的恋爱过程非常短暂。

sentences.en: And they move in together.
sentences.zh: 然后他们就同居了。

sentences.en: And she realizes that he is also physically abusive.
sentences.zh: 她发现他也有暴力倾向。

sentences.en: Once she becomes pregnant, he becomes enraged and beats her up very badly.
sentences.zh: 她怀孕后，他变得暴跳如雷，把她打得很惨。

sentences.en: The police come.
sentences.zh: 警察来了。

sentences.en: Windows are broken.
sentences.zh: 窗户被打碎了。

sentences.en: Plates are smashed.
sentences.zh: 盘子被砸烂了。

sentences.en: She's lost consciousness.
sentences.zh: 她失去了知觉。

sentences.en: And she flees back to her mother's house.
sentences.zh: 于是她逃回了母亲家。

sentences.en: 15 years old.
sentences.zh: 才15岁。

sentences.en: Yeah, she just turned 16.

sentences.en: So Norma goes to work in bars as a bartender.
sentences.zh: 于是诺玛开始在酒吧当调酒师。

sentences.en: She's drinking a lot at this point.
sentences.zh: 那时候她酗酒很厉害。

sentences.en: And she gets pregnant two more times.
sentences.zh: 后来她又怀孕了两次。

sentences.en: Her second pregnancy, she gives the baby up for adoption.
sentences.zh: 第二次怀孕时，她把孩子送人领养了。

sentences.en: And when she gets pregnant the third time, she's working as a carnival barker in a traveling carnival in Louisiana and Mississippi.
sentences.zh: 第三次怀孕时，她在路易斯安那州和密西西比州的一个流动嘉年华里当招揽员。

sentences.en: They've come to a stop for the winter, actually, in Florida.
sentences.zh: 当时嘉年华在佛罗里达州停下来过冬。

sentences.en: And she realizes that she's pregnant.
sentences.zh: 她意识到自己怀孕了。

sentences.en: She feels the familiar queasiness and tiredness.
sentences.zh: 她感到了那种熟悉的恶心和疲惫。

sentences.en: At this point, she really, really doesn't want to go through the pregnancy and having the baby and giving the baby up for adoption again.
sentences.zh: 此时此刻，她真的、真的不想再经历怀孕、生子，然后再次把孩子送人领养的过程了。

sentences.en: She wanted to save herself that emotional and physical anguish.
sentences.zh: 她想让自己免受那种情感和身体上的痛苦。

sentences.en: And she gathers all the money that she has in her pockets, buys a bus ticket, and ends up back in Dallas again.
sentences.zh: 于是她掏出兜里所有的钱，买了一张车票，最后又回到了达拉斯。

sentences.en: So she's pretty desperate and she's looking for any solution.
sentences.zh: 她当时非常绝望，正在寻找任何解决办法。

sentences.en: I mean, she wants to get rid of this pregnancy.
sentences.zh: 我是说，她想终止这次妊娠。

sentences.en: So she's talking to someone in the bar, a woman named Jinx, who's a friend.
sentences.zh: 于是她和酒吧里的一个人聊天，那是一个叫金克斯的朋友。

sentences.en: And Jinx tells her there's something called abortion.
sentences.zh: 金克斯告诉她有一种东西叫堕胎。

sentences.en: It's this medical procedure that doctors use to end a pregnancy.
sentences.zh: 这是医生用来终止妊娠的一种医疗程序。

sentences.en: What you need to understand about this period is that it's really, really different from the one we live in today.
sentences.zh: 关于那个时期，你需要了解的是，它与我们今天生活的时代真的非常非常不同。

sentences.en: Abortion is not the culture war's issue yet.
sentences.zh: 堕胎当时还不是文化战争的议题。

sentences.en: It hadn't become this lightning rod that it would become later.
sentences.zh: 它还没有成为后来那种引发激烈争议的焦点。

sentences.en: It wasn't yet the defining issue around which our modern American political landscape kind of took shape.
sentences.zh: 它还不是塑造我们现代美国政治格局的决定性议题。

sentences.en: So back in the 1960s, most polls had Americans thinking that some form of abortion probably should be legal.
sentences.zh: 所以回到20世纪60年代，大多数民意调查显示，美国人认为某种形式的堕胎应该是合法的。

sentences.en: It was seen as a kind of women's health initiative.
sentences.zh: 它被视为一种女性健康倡议。

sentences.en: And it was seen as a kind of effort at reform.
sentences.zh: 也被视为一种改革努力。

sentences.en: I mean, these were laws that were seen by a lot of upper middle class and middle class people as sort of inhumane.
sentences.zh: 我是说，许多中产阶级和中上层阶级的人认为这些法律有些不人道。

sentences.en: You know, women dying from botched illegal abortions and also kind of outdated.
sentences.zh: 你知道，女性因为非法堕胎手术失败而死亡，而且这些法律也有些过时了。

sentences.en: This sort of a relic of the paSt.
sentences.zh: 这算是一种过去的遗迹。

sentences.en: These were Victorian era laws still governing policy in modern America.
sentences.zh: 这些维多利亚时代的法律依然在现代美国支配着政策。

sentences.en: The laws on abortion vary from state to state.
sentences.zh: 堕胎法律因州而异。

sentences.en: Three states, Washington, Alaska and Hawaii, have abortion laws somewhat similar to New York's.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿州、阿拉斯加州和夏威夷州这三个州的堕胎法与纽约州的有些相似。

sentences.en: So because of all of that, what was happening around the country was that there were these bills in state legislatures aimed at decriminalizing abortion.
sentences.zh: 所以正因如此，全国各地都在发生这样的情况：州议会中出现了一些旨在将堕胎合法化的法案。

sentences.en: Thirteen states have laws permitting legal abortion in certain circumstances.
sentences.zh: 有十三个州制定了在特定情况下允许合法堕胎的法律。

sentences.en: They called them liberalization bills, where instead of no access at all, these bills would allow some.
sentences.zh: 他们称之为自由化法案，即不再是完全禁止，而是允许在一定程度上进行堕胎。

sentences.en: And in some cases, a lot.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，甚至允许很大程度上的堕胎。

sentences.en: For example, in New York state.
sentences.zh: 例如，在纽约州。

sentences.en: The New York state Senate today passed one of the nation's most sweeping abortion control bills.
sentences.zh: 纽约州参议院今天通过了全国最广泛的堕胎控制法案之一。

sentences.en: The really surprising twist is that a Republican governor signed it into law.
sentences.zh: 真正令人惊讶的转折是，一位共和党州长签署了该法案使其成为法律。

sentences.en: And this was not unusual, because the places where these laws are being talked about, the places where they actually pass, tend to be run by Republicans.
sentences.zh: 这并不罕见，因为讨论这些法律的地方，以及这些法律真正通过的地方，往往是由共和党人管理的。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: In California, actor Ronald Reagan and Mrs. Reagan arrived to cast their votes in the state's primary election.
sentences.zh: 在加利福尼亚州，演员罗纳德·里根和里根夫人抵达现场，在州初选中投下了选票。

sentences.en: He's the Republican nominee for governor.
sentences.zh: 他是共和党的州长候选人。

sentences.en: It's his first political conteSt.
sentences.zh: 这是他第一次参加政治竞选。

sentences.en: I mean, most surprisingly, so I was going through and doing this research,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，最令人惊讶的是，当时我正在深入研究这些资料，

sentences.en: and I read about California and saw that the person who signed the California bill into law in 1967 was Ronald Reagan.
sentences.zh: 我读到了关于加利福尼亚州的内容，发现1967年签署加州堕胎法案使其成为法律的人是罗纳德·里根。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Colorado's bill passed in 1967.
sentences.zh: 科罗拉多州的法案于1967年通过。

sentences.en: North Carolina's in 1967.
sentences.zh: 北卡罗来纳州是在1967年。

sentences.en: Georgia in 1968.
sentences.zh: 佐治亚州是在1968年。

sentences.en: Maryland in 1968.
sentences.zh: 马里兰州是在1968年。

sentences.en: Kansas in 1969.
sentences.zh: 堪萨斯州是在1969年。

sentences.en: Arkansas in 1969.
sentences.zh: 阿肯色州是在1969年。

sentences.en: New Mexico in 1969.
sentences.zh: 新墨西哥州是在1969年。

sentences.en: Virginia in 1970.
sentences.zh: 弗吉尼亚州是在1970年。

sentences.en: South Carolina in 1970.
sentences.zh: 南卡罗来纳州是在1970年。

sentences.en: Wow, so these politics are kind of unrecognizable to us now.
sentences.zh: 哇，所以这些政治立场在今天看来简直让人难以置信。

sentences.en: This was actually very surprising to me.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说确实非常令人惊讶。

sentences.en: I didn't understand this history before I started.
sentences.zh: 在开始研究之前，我并不了解这段历史。

sentences.en: And I almost felt like I was blindfolded.
sentences.zh: 我感觉自己就像被蒙住了眼睛一样。

sentences.en: Like, I couldn't tell who would make what decision.
sentences.zh: 就好像，我无法判断谁会做出什么样的决定。

sentences.en: It was like, like, I had this key to understanding politics today, the way I understand left and right and Democrat and Republican, and none of that worked.
sentences.zh: 就像我掌握了理解当今政治的钥匙，我所理解的左派、右派、民主党和共和党，在当时完全行不通。

sentences.en: It was an entirely different map.
sentences.zh: 那是一张完全不同的地图。

sentences.en: The only part of the country that failed in passing these bills was the Northeast, Massachusetts, Maine, Connecticut, Rhode Island.
sentences.zh: 全国唯一未能通过这些法案的地区是东北部，包括马萨诸塞州、缅因州、康涅狄格州和罗德岛州。

sentences.en: And the reason for that is that the biggest and fiercest opposition to abortion was from the Catholic Church and Catholic activists.
sentences.zh: 原因在于，当时对堕胎最强烈、最激进的反对力量来自天主教会和天主教活动人士。

sentences.en: And Catholics, for the most part, were Democrats.
sentences.zh: 而天主教徒在很大程度上是民主党人。

sentences.en: So those states that are still solidly Catholic and Democratic.
sentences.zh: 所以那些州至今仍是坚定的天主教和民主党阵地。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: But one state that had yet to do any of this, that hadn't liberalized yet, was Texas.
sentences.zh: 但有一个州尚未采取任何行动，还没有实现自由化，那就是得克萨斯州。

sentences.en: And Texas was the state that Norma was living in when she got pregnant for a third time and went to her friend Jinx at the bar to ask for advice in how to deal with it.
sentences.zh: 诺玛第三次怀孕时就住在得克萨斯州，她去酒吧找朋友金克斯寻求建议，想知道该如何处理。

sentences.en: Didn't want to have it.
sentences.zh: 我不想要这个孩子。

sentences.en: Didn't want it in my body.
sentences.zh: 我不希望它在我的身体里。

sentences.en: Didn't want it in my body.
sentences.zh: 我不希望它在我的身体里。

sentences.en: I wanted to have an abortion.
sentences.zh: 我想堕胎。

sentences.en: So Norma finds out that there's this thing called abortion.
sentences.zh: 于是诺玛发现有“堕胎”这回事。

sentences.en: And she goes to her doctor, very kindly elderly man, who actually delivered her first two children.
sentences.zh: 她去找她的医生，那是一位非常和蔼的老人，她前两个孩子就是他接生的。

sentences.en: And she said she's heard about abortion and she wants to have one.
sentences.zh: 她说她听说过堕胎，想要做一次。

sentences.en: And he looks at her with kind of patient eyes and says, I'm sorry, Norma, you can't get an abortion in the state of Texas.
sentences.zh: 他用一种耐心的眼神看着她说：“抱歉，诺玛，在得克萨斯州你不能堕胎。”

sentences.en: It's illegal.
sentences.zh: 这是违法的。

sentences.en: And she's really upset by this.
sentences.zh: 她对此感到非常难过。

sentences.en: And she says, isn't there some way?
sentences.zh: 她说：“难道就没有什么办法吗？”

sentences.en: I mean, won't somebody do it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，难道就没有人愿意做吗？

sentences.en: Here, I can give you money.
sentences.zh: 我可以给你钱。

sentences.en: And he says, you know, it's not about money.
sentences.zh: 他说：“你知道，这不是钱的问题。”

sentences.en: I'm supposed to report a doctor who does it.
sentences.zh: 我有义务举报做这种手术的医生。

sentences.en: It's illegal, Norma.
sentences.zh: 这是违法的，诺玛。

sentences.en: And so at some point in the visit, he writes down a name on a piece of paper.
sentences.zh: 在就诊的某个时刻，他在一张纸上写下了一个名字。

sentences.en: And she gets kind of excited because she thinks, oh, maybe this is actually the name of someone who will do an abortion for me that he just doesn't want to say out loud.
sentences.zh: 她感到有些兴奋，因为她想，哦，这可能就是那个愿意为我堕胎的人的名字，只是他不想大声说出来。

sentences.en: And when she calls it later, she realizes it's the name and number of an adoption lawyer.
sentences.zh: 后来她打电话过去时，才发现那是领养律师的名字和电话。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So he's trying to dissuade her.
sentences.zh: 所以他是在劝她放弃。

sentences.en: He's trying to dissuade her.
sentences.zh: 他是在劝她放弃。

sentences.en: She decides she's just going to take the matter into her own hands.
sentences.zh: 她决定自己想办法解决。

sentences.en: And she gets a recommendation from a friend about an illegal abortion provider.
sentences.zh: 她从朋友那里得到了一个非法堕胎提供者的推荐。

sentences.en: And she thinks she's going to do it.
sentences.zh: 她以为她能做成这件事。

sentences.en: So she saves up some money.
sentences.zh: 于是她攒了一些钱。

sentences.en: I had $250 of my rent money saved up.
sentences.zh: 我攒了250美元的房租钱。

sentences.en: And she goes to the address that the person gave her.
sentences.zh: 她去了那个人给她的地址。

sentences.en: And she knocks on a door and she goes in.
sentences.zh: 她敲了敲门，然后走了进去。

sentences.en: And the account in her book is that she sees blood on the floor and police tape and no one's there.
sentences.zh: 她在书中的描述是，她看到地板上有血迹，还有警察拉起的警戒线，里面空无一人。

sentences.en: There was nobody there.
sentences.zh: 那里一个人也没有。

sentences.en: And she sees someone kind of nearby this building and asks what happened.
sentences.zh: 她看到附近有个人，就问发生了什么事。

sentences.en: And he said, oh, the cops raided this place a couple of weeks ago.
sentences.zh: 他说：“哦，警察几周前突袭了这个地方。”

sentences.en: And she's terrified and she thinks she just can't go through with something like that.
sentences.zh: 她吓坏了，觉得这种事她实在做不来。

sentences.en: So she calls the adoption lawyer in desperation.
sentences.zh: 于是她绝望地给那位领养律师打了电话。

sentences.en: And the lawyer, as it turns out, is friends with someone named Linda Coffey.
sentences.zh: 结果发现，这位律师和一位名叫琳达·科菲的人是朋友。

sentences.en: He said that he just knew of these two young law students who just graduated college.
sentences.zh: 他说他刚好认识两名刚从大学毕业的年轻法学院学生。

sentences.en: Linda Coffey.
sentences.zh: 琳达·科菲。

sentences.en: And she, together with another young woman lawyer.
sentences.zh: 她和另一位年轻的女律师在一起。

sentences.en: Sarah Weddington.
sentences.zh: 莎拉·威丁顿。

sentences.en: Sarah Weddington.
sentences.zh: 莎拉·威丁顿。

sentences.en: Women are looking for a case that would challenge the abortion laws for the whole country to bring to the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 这些女性正在寻找一个可以挑战全国堕胎法的案件，以便将其诉至最高法院。

sentences.en: I mean, it just went right over my head.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我当时完全没听懂。

sentences.en: I mean, I didn't have a clue to what he was saying.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我根本不知道他在说什么。

sentences.en: And would I like to meet these two women?
sentences.zh: “你想见见这两位女士吗？”

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: These two young women lawyers are feminists.
sentences.zh: 这两位年轻的女律师都是女权主义者。

sentences.en: Linda Coffey has clerked for a very famous feminist judge.
sentences.zh: 琳达·科菲曾为一位非常著名的女权主义法官担任过书记员。

sentences.en: And Sarah Weddington has been seared by her own experience at having to go to Mexico to get an abortion when she got pregnant in law school.
sentences.zh: 而莎拉·威丁顿则因自己在法学院怀孕时不得不去墨西哥堕胎的经历而深受创伤。

sentences.en: And they're really, at this point, not that much older than Norma, who's in her very early 20s.
sentences.zh: 当时她们其实比诺玛大不了多少，诺玛那时才二十出头。

sentences.en: And when she first meets Sarah and Linda at a pizza restaurant in Dallas called Columbo's, she says it has checkered tablecloths.
sentences.zh: 当她在达拉斯一家叫科伦坡的披萨店第一次见到莎拉和琳达时，她说店里铺着格子桌布。

sentences.en: She's already a few months pregnant.
sentences.zh: 她当时已经怀孕几个月了。

sentences.en: We sat and talked and drank beer for the longest time.
sentences.zh: 我们坐着聊了很久，喝了啤酒。

sentences.en: We got kind of smashed.
sentences.zh: 我们喝得有点醉了。

sentences.en: Then we had pizza.
sentences.zh: 然后我们吃了披萨。

sentences.en: Then we drank some more beer.
sentences.zh: 接着又喝了一些啤酒。

sentences.en: And they started pounding, you know, all this, well, don't you think women should have the right to control their own body?
sentences.zh: 她们开始不断强调，你知道，就是那种“难道你不认为女性应该有权掌控自己的身体吗？”

sentences.en: Yeah!
sentences.zh: 没错！

sentences.en: So what was it about Norma that attracted these lawyers to her?
sentences.zh: 那么，诺玛身上有什么特质吸引了这些律师呢？

sentences.en: What made her, in their mind, the perfect plaintiff for this case?
sentences.zh: 在她们看来，是什么让她成为了这个案件的完美原告？

sentences.en: So in a narrow legal sense, Norma actually really worked.
sentences.zh: 从狭义的法律角度来看，诺玛确实很合适。

sentences.en: She was a young woman who desperately wanted an abortion and had asked her doctor for one.
sentences.zh: 她是一位迫切想要堕胎并向医生求助的年轻女性。

sentences.en: But it just so happened that she lived in a state that did not allow it legally.
sentences.zh: 但恰好她住在一个法律禁止堕胎的州。

sentences.en: So in that sense, she fit the bill.
sentences.zh: 所以从这个意义上说，她符合条件。

sentences.en: But in so many other senses, in a very broad way, she didn't.
sentences.zh: 但在许多其他方面，从更广泛的角度来看，她并不合适。

sentences.en: She was very imperfect.
sentences.zh: 她很不完美。

sentences.en: And she was kind of a loose cannon and kind of rough.
sentences.zh: 她有点像个不受控制的“散兵游勇”，性格也比较粗鲁。

sentences.en: All I was was just a simple hello girl from Louisiana who thought she knew what she wanted.
sentences.zh: 我不过是个来自路易斯安那州的普通女孩，以为自己知道自己想要什么。

sentences.en: She was a very flawed spokeswoman for this movement.
sentences.zh: 她是这场运动中一个非常有缺陷的代言人。

sentences.en: But despite all of that, the two lawyers brought the case, Weddington and Coffey.
sentences.zh: 但尽管如此，这两位律师——威丁顿和科菲——还是提起了诉讼。

sentences.en: Mr. Chief Justice, and may it please the court, we are once again before this court to ask relief against the continued enforcement of the Texas Abortion Statute.
sentences.zh: 首席大法官先生，法庭请允许，我们再次来到法庭，请求救济，以反对得克萨斯州堕胎法规的持续执行。

sentences.en: The first plaintiff was Jane Roe, an unmarried pregnant girl who had sought an abortion in the state of Texas
sentences.zh: 第一位原告是简·罗，一名未婚怀孕的女孩，她曾在得克萨斯州寻求堕胎，

sentences.en: and was denied it because of the Texas Abortion Statute, which provides an abortionist lawful only for the purpose of saving the life of the woman.
sentences.zh: 但因得克萨斯州堕胎法规而被拒绝，该法规规定只有为了挽救孕妇生命时，堕胎才是合法的。

sentences.en: The women of Texas still must either travel to other states, if they are that sophisticated and can't afford it, or they must resort to some other very undesirable alternatives.
sentences.zh: 得克萨斯州的女性仍然必须要么前往其他州（如果她们有足够的经济能力和见识），要么只能诉诸其他非常不可取的替代方案。

sentences.en: And yet we can certainly show that it is a continuing problem to Texas women.
sentences.zh: 然而，我们完全可以证明，这对得克萨斯州的女性来说是一个持续存在的问题。

sentences.en: There still are unwanted pregnancies.
sentences.zh: 意外怀孕的情况依然存在。

sentences.en: There are still women who, for various reasons, do not wish to continue the pregnancy, whether because of personal health considerations, whether because of their family situation,
sentences.zh: 仍然有女性因为各种原因不希望继续怀孕，无论是出于个人健康考虑，还是因为家庭状况，

sentences.en: whether because of financial situations, education, working situations, some of the many things we discussed at the last hearing.
sentences.zh: 或者是出于经济状况、教育、工作情况，以及我们在上次听证会上讨论过的许多其他问题。

sentences.en: And they won.
sentences.zh: 她们赢了。

sentences.en: And they changed the lives of millions of women.
sentences.zh: 她们改变了数百万女性的生活。

sentences.en: Good evening.
sentences.zh: 晚上好。

sentences.en: In a landmark ruling, the Supreme Court today legalized abortions.
sentences.zh: 在今天的一项里程碑式裁决中，最高法院将堕胎合法化了。

sentences.en: So the court rules seven to two in favor of Roe.
sentences.zh: 法院以七比二的投票结果支持了罗诉韦德案。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: That's a overwhelming majority that's almost inconceivable at this moment.
sentences.zh: 这是一个压倒性的多数，在今天看来几乎是不可想象的。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: But at the time, it was seen as really kind of uncontroversial.
sentences.zh: 但在当时，这被认为是非常没有争议的。

sentences.en: It's nothing like the firestorms that were created after Brown versus Board of Education in 1954, which desegregated schools, or the 1962 decision banning prayer in schools.
sentences.zh: 它完全不像1954年布朗诉教育委员会案（该案废除了学校种族隔离）或1962年禁止学校祈祷的裁决那样引发了轩然大波。

sentences.en: Nothing like that.
sentences.zh: 完全不像那样。

sentences.en: It just kind of passed.
sentences.zh: 它就这样通过了。

sentences.en: The majority in cases from Texas and Georgia said that the decision to end a pregnancy during the first three months belongs to the woman and her doctor, not the government.
sentences.zh: 得克萨斯州和佐治亚州案件的多数派意见认为，在怀孕前三个月终止妊娠的决定权属于女性及其医生，而非政府。

sentences.en: Justice Harry Blackmun writes the majority opinion for the court.
sentences.zh: 哈里·布莱克门大法官撰写了法院的多数意见书。

sentences.en: He's a Nixon appointee, and he used to work for the Mayo Clinic representing doctors.
sentences.zh: 他是尼克松任命的，曾为梅奥诊所工作，代表医生利益。

sentences.en: He was their general counsel.
sentences.zh: 他曾担任他们的总法律顾问。

sentences.en: He's from Minnesota.
sentences.zh: 他来自明尼苏达州。

sentences.en: He's really coming from the perspective of doctors.
sentences.zh: 他确实是从医生的角度出发的。

sentences.en: You know, it's a doctor's prerogative to make decisions that are best for his patient, and the state really shouldn't get in the way of that.
sentences.zh: 你知道，做出对病人最有利的决定是医生的特权，政府确实不应该干预。

sentences.en: This is essentially a right to privacy.
sentences.zh: 这本质上是一种隐私权。

sentences.en: And this right to privacy, he says, is a constitutional right.
sentences.zh: 他说，这种隐私权是一种宪法权利。

sentences.en: There's a lot of scholarship about that that comes later.
sentences.zh: 后来有很多关于此的学术研究。

sentences.en: But at the time, this is what he decides.
sentences.zh: 但在当时，这就是他的决定。

sentences.en: This is what the court decides.
sentences.zh: 这就是法院的决定。

sentences.en: But it's unquestioned.
sentences.zh: 但这并没有受到质疑。

sentences.en: Romain ought to have created a social firestorm.
sentences.zh: 罗诉韦德案本应引发一场社会风暴。

sentences.en: But policy-wise, it was a really big change.
sentences.zh: 但在政策层面，这确实是一个巨大的变化。

sentences.en: Now, suddenly, 46 states had to revise their laws based on this federal ruling, and that was a big policy change.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，46个州不得不根据这项联邦裁决修改法律，这是一个重大的政策转变。

sentences.en: So it became suddenly a national issue.
sentences.zh: 所以它突然变成了一个全国性的议题。

sentences.en: And it became a national issue in the way that it had never been before.
sentences.zh: 它以一种前所未有的方式成为了全国性议题。

sentences.en: Before it had been a matter of what any given state was going to decide.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，这只是任何一个州自行决定的事情。

sentences.en: You know, there has to be a meaning.
sentences.zh: 你知道，生活必须有意义。

sentences.en: Every boy in this society is raised to be something.
sentences.zh: 这个社会中的每个男孩从小就被培养要成为某种人。

sentences.en: To be a doctor, to be a lawyer, to be something.
sentences.zh: 成为医生，成为律师，成为某种人。

sentences.en: Every girl is raised to be a housewife and a mother.
sentences.zh: 而每个女孩从小就被培养要成为家庭主妇和母亲。

sentences.en: She is not raised to be something other than that.
sentences.zh: 她没有被培养去成为除此之外的任何人。

sentences.en: And it became a national issue exactly at the time that the feminist movement and feminism were asking for their own rights.
sentences.zh: 它成为全国性议题的时间，恰好是女权运动和女权主义者争取自身权利的时候。

sentences.en: Is this the true role?
sentences.zh: 这就是真正的角色吗？

sentences.en: Do I have to get married?
sentences.zh: 我必须结婚吗？

sentences.en: Do I have to get pregnant?
sentences.zh: 我必须怀孕吗？

sentences.en: Do I have a choice?
sentences.zh: 我有选择权吗？

sentences.en: Women in America were pushing the Equal Rights Amendment, were marching and saying our bodies ourselves.
sentences.zh: 美国的女性正在推动《平等权利修正案》，她们游行并高呼“我们的身体，我们自己”。

sentences.en: We love to change the conditions that oppress us.
sentences.zh: 我们热爱改变那些压迫我们的条件。

sentences.en: They've said what we're saying, that women have a fundamental right to control their own bodies and to control their own lives.
sentences.zh: 她们说了我们正在说的话，即女性拥有掌控自己身体和生活的根本权利。

sentences.en: And so abortion, that started to become fused in the public's mind with feminism.
sentences.zh: 因此，堕胎在公众心目中开始与女权主义融合在一起。

sentences.en: Are the lucky
sentences.zh: 是幸运的

sentences.en: And it begins to become this lightning rod,
sentences.zh: 它开始成为一个避雷针，

sentences.en: one that would change the nature and the fate of this issue entirely.
sentences.zh: 一个将彻底改变这一议题的性质和命运的避雷针。

sentences.en: We are not here to advocate abortion.
sentences.zh: 我们来此并非为了倡导堕胎。

sentences.en: We do not ask this court to rule that abortion is good or desirable in any particular situation.
sentences.zh: 我们并未要求法庭裁定堕胎在任何特定情况下是好的或可取的。

sentences.en: We are here to advocate that the decision as to whether or not a particular woman will continue to carry or will terminate a pregnancy
sentences.zh: 我们来此是为了主张，关于某位女性是否继续怀孕或终止妊娠的决定，

sentences.en: is a decision that should be made by that individual.
sentences.zh: 应当由该个人自行做出。

sentences.en: That in fact she has a constitutional right to make that decision for herself and that the state has shown no interest in interfering with that decision.
sentences.zh: 事实上，她拥有为自己做出这一决定的宪法权利，而政府并无理由干涉这一决定。

sentences.en: Our supplemental brief on page 14 points out that the brief of the opposition can't fight the side when life doesn't.
sentences.zh: 我们在第14页的补充摘要中指出，对方的摘要无法在生命权缺失时进行辩驳。

sentences.en: In part two, the culture wars and Norman McCorvey's complicated role in them.
sentences.zh: 在第二部分中，我们将探讨文化战争以及诺玛·麦考维在其中扮演的复杂角色。

sentences.zh: 本期节目由琳赛·加里森制作，丽莎·托宾和佩奇·考维特编辑。

sentences.en: It was engineered by Chris Wood and Dan Powell.
sentences.zh: 由克里斯·伍德和丹·鲍威尔负责工程录制。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Landsberg of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由Wonderly乐队的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰兹伯格创作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》节目，我们将为您准备假期接待客人的相关事宜。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 敬请收听，获取让客人宾至如归的小贴士。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是需要全黑环境才能入睡的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they black out to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是否喝到断片才能睡着。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们对光线有什么要求？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们是喝咖啡还是喝茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？
